candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines WQBELs as water-quality-based effluent limitations; how this label is applied when matching reported measurements to permit limits affects which numeric limits are treated as enforceable WQBELs versus other limit categories.

Equates the WET acronym with whole effluent toxicity; a different reading of WET references elsewhere would change which toxicity-related numeric limits apply (A) and which whole-effluent-toxicity monitoring requirements are in scope (B).

Defines WLA as waste-load allocation; interpretation of allocation-based limit language in the permit depends on this meaning and could change which derived numeric discharge limits are identified as applicable.

Identifies WQMP as the Water Quality Management Plan; whether limits or monitoring obligations are sourced from the WQMP versus other authorities depends on this definition and could change applicable limit and monitoring determinations.

candidates.exact_span: As used in this document, references to State water quality standards and/or rules, regulations and/or management plans may mean the State of New Mexico and/or Tribal or both.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The permissive 'may mean' and 'and/or Tribal or both' wording leaves ambiguous whether NM state, tribal, or combined standards, rules, regulations, and management plans govern; different readings would change which numeric limits apply (A), which monitoring requirements bind (B), and how missing or conditional monitoring is classified when jurisdictional applicability is unclear (C).
